_comment: Exercises the policy pack examples/policies/human-signoff.json; the inline policy is byte-for-byte that descriptor (asserted by scripts/validate-json.sh). See docs/policy-packs.md.
description: Decision Mode policy pack 'human sign-off': only the designated human approver may emit the Commitment; the initiator and an approving agent are FORBIDDEN.

policy.description: Human sign-off: agents propose, evaluate and vote, but only the designated human approver may emit the Commitment that binds the decision. Select this policy at SessionStart for the sessions that need a human; the selection rule itself (for example an amount above a limit) is not expressible inside a policy. Replace agent://human-approver with the approver's authenticated sender identity.

payload.rationale: vendor invoice of 25,000 USD, above the deployment's sign-off limit

messages._comment: Agents still deliberate and vote. Under voting.algorithm 'none' the ballots are recorded but no voting constraint is enforced; the human's Commitment is what binds.

payload.reason: initiator tries to seal its own proposal

messages._comment: commitment.authority 'designated_role' replaces the initiator's default Commitment authority (RFC-MACP-0007 Section 2.1 authority matrix; RFC-MACP-0012 Section 4). The initiator is not in designated_roles, so it is an unauthorized sender.

payload.reason: an approving agent tries to seal the decision

messages._comment: A declared participant that voted APPROVE is still not a designated committer.
The designated human approver is the only sender whose Commitment is accepted.
